### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/action-handler-coordinate.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**6** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/action-handler-coordinate.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 24f2f4014d0c9bbd43ec6928942fa44b21c1dff6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `699b186e50e529a73081207e5a948d63fe60838f` — the merge of head `efef4782e2d3383e25e732b74136739929681d0e` into base `24f2f4014d0c9bbd43ec6928942fa44b21c1dff6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 699b186e50e529a73081207e5a948d63fe60838f && git checkout 699b186e50e529a73081207e5a948d63fe60838f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 24f2f4014d0c9bbd43ec6928942fa44b21c1dff6 efef4782e2d3383e25e732b74136739929681d0e && git checkout -B drift-repro 24f2f4014d0c9bbd43ec6928942fa44b21c1dff6 && git merge --no-ff efef4782e2d3383e25e732b74136739929681d0e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 24f2f4014d0c9bbd43ec6928942fa44b21c1dff6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 24f2f4014d0c9bbd43ec6928942fa44b21c1dff6` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `ab806df240348e20541288f4a5b4d803d7304563`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

- `isArtifactShippedAction` now skips an authored row only when some holder's artifact owns the row's object (`standaloneActionOwnsRoute`: same owner key, or an object-less artifact). Checked the edge the table does not list: an object-less environment row (owner key `global`) beside a holder's artifact on `account` is now bound under `metadata-service`; dispatch at `/actions/account/approve` still probes `account` first (the holder's handler), and only objects no holder owns fall through to the environment's `global` handler (`actionHandlerObjectKeys`). Correct under D4.
- `artifactActionsNamed`: the bare-name first match plus each holder's own artifact (`packageScopedHoldersOf(..., { includeDisabledPackages: true })`), deduplicated by identity. Disabled holders keep their object. Matches the stated rule.
- **should-fix S1 — the override base is still picked by list order when two artifacts share the row's owner key.** `isDeclaredArtifactActionOverride` takes `artifacts.find((a) => standaloneActionOwnerKey(a) === objectKey)`. For two holders whose `approve` is object-less (both key `global`), `find` returns the first by registration/bare-name order, so a declared `B.custom` override of B's object-less action is judged against A (`isServedOverrideRowOf(row, A, installed)` → false) and stays unbound, B's body runs. That is row 3's defect in the object-less shape. Fix (small, fold here): among artifacts at the row's owner key, take the one whose `_packageId` equals `action.overrides?.package` when given; with several and no package named, do not pick (return false and say so once). Add a pin with two object-less holders in both registration orders.
- Row 2 (one holder, environment row on another object: not found → the environment's body runs): resolution and the declaration the route serves are unchanged (`#32365` case 1); only the missing handler is added. I read it as within the epic's "one-holder behaviour unchanged" red line (a dispatch that failed now runs the declared item); seat may confirm.
- `action-handler-coordinate.ts`: docblock only, matches the code.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/objectql: patch`; `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right (dispatches that answered not-found now run the declared body; no refusal added, no export/schema moves). `Metadata-protocol: none` holds.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Author login `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay); area E2b. Hot shared file `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts` (A4/E2b/E1 per amendment 6): confirm no other open PR edits `isArtifactShippedAction` / `isDeclaredArtifactActionOverride` before landing.
- CI not complete when read; the ACCEPT re-reads every check at the landing head.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `efef4782e2d3383e25e732b74136739929681d0e`
Local-runs: none

Delta over my FAIL at `ab806df240348e20541288f4a5b4d803d7304563` (comment 6879713494). The diff `ab806df2...efef4782` has two commits and touches `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts` and `plugin-authored-actions.test.ts`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **S1 fixed.** `isDeclaredArtifactActionOverride` no longer takes `artifacts.find(...)` by list order. Among the artifacts at the row's owner key, it takes the one whose `_packageId` is the row's `overrides.package`. A lone holder at the key is taken as before, so one-holder behaviour is unchanged. With several holders and none named, it picks no base: the row is bound as no override, and a once-per-process `warn` names the holders and the fix ("name the base package in the row's overrides.package"). That matches the ADR-0150 red line "ambiguity reported, never guessed".
- **Pin.** Two object-less holders (both keyed `global`), a declared override of B, in both registration orders: B runs the override and A runs its own body. Before the fix, the "B then A" order is the case that bound against the wrong base.
- **Test double.** The booted-kernel row-store `find` now honours `ast.limit`, so the double no longer answers more rows than the caller bounded. That is a test-only change and it tightens fidelity.
- A row naming a package that is not among several holders at its key gets no base and is reported. A row naming a package other than a lone holder is judged by `isServedOverrideRowOf` against that holder, as before.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged from the first record: `@objectstack/objectql: patch`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. The new no-base outcome only arises with several holders at one key, which the first record already treated as the per-holder widening.

### ③ Boundary flags

- CI at this head when read (16:58Z): 33 success, 16 skipped, 1 in progress, none red. The ACCEPT re-reads every check at the landing head.
